info.title: relay-queue
info.summary: The message queue between the human and his agents.
info.description:
A minimal, durable, local-only HTTP task queue with a mobile web UI. Every mutation is appended to `data/events.jsonl` (write + fsync) BEFORE the response is sent, then replayed into memory on boot. The core server has zero runtime dependencies.

THIS DOCUMENT IS HAND-WRITTEN AND DRIFT-CHECKED. `openapi.json` is the source of truth; `openapi.yaml` is generated from it by `node openapi-yaml.js`. `tools/openapi-selftest.js` boots a real server, proves every path+method documented here actually routes, and scans `server.js` for route segments that are NOT documented here. Add a route, and that suite fails until this file grows with it.

CONVENTIONS THAT HOLD EVERYWHERE

- No authentication. The server binds 127.0.0.1 by default and trusts every caller. Do not expose it.
- JSON in, JSON out, `cache-control: no-store`, except for the static UI, the icons, the image bytes and `/tts`.
- Request bodies are decoded with a STRICT UTF-8 decoder. A body that is not valid UTF-8 is refused 400 (`the request body is not valid UTF-8, so nothing was stored`) with a `detail` object naming the first bad byte. NOTHING IS STORED. Build bodies with `curl --data-binary @file.json`, never with a shell-quoted `-d` string.
- Text that already contains U+FFFD (a replacement character - the damage happened before it got here) is refused 400 on agent-written routes (`/messages`, `/tasks/{id}/result`, `/tasks/{id}/progress`, `/credits/*`). `POST /tasks` is the exception: it WARNS AND STORES, because that is the route the human's own typed and dictated messages arrive on and dropping one would be worse than the damage.
- An EMPTY body is a valid `{}`. `POST /tasks/{id}/claim` and `POST /tasks/{id}/progress` depend on that.
- Bodies are capped at 1 MiB (413). `instruction`/`text` is capped at 8000 chars; a progress `note` at 500.
- List filters: `conversation` is canonical, `conversationId` is accepted everywhere as an alias. `since` takes ISO 8601 or epoch milliseconds and is STRICTLY after. `limit` must be a non-negative integer.
- Wrong method on a real path is 405 with `{ allow }`. An unknown path is 404 `no route for <METHOD> <path>`.

THE TRAPS, IN ONE PLACE (each is repeated on the operation it bites)

1. `POST /tasks/{id}/claim` with NO identity field returns 200 with `claimedBy: null`. The seat then reads occupied with nobody in it, the real worker cannot renew its own lease, and the task never returns to `pending`. Always send `by`.
2. `POST /tasks/{id}/result` is one-shot. 409 if already done, 400 if `result` is null, 409 if `by` names someone other than the holder. Omit `by` to answer a task whose claim is orphaned.
3. Never `POST /tasks/{id}/relayed` before the `result` POST returned 200.
4. `/checklist` (singular) and `/checklists` (plural) are DIFFERENT SYSTEMS one letter apart.
5. `POST /conversations/{id}` answers 409 when the patch it just applied was overwritten inside its own request. Nothing you asked for is in effect.
6. `agentLeftReason: "presumed-gone"` is reserved for the vacant-chair sweep and is refused 400 from callers.
7. `DELETE /conversations/{id}/share` is destructive, and revoke-then-republish mints a NEW slug. Re-POST to refresh instead.
8. `pick` events never reach the SSE stream. `check` events do.
9. The word `agent` means three different things on three routes. See `POST /tasks/{id}/claim`.

Rendered rather than read from the `openapi.yaml` file so the two can never disagree: the file on disk exists for git and for tooling that wants a path, and `node openapi-yaml.js` regenerates it. `tools/openapi-selftest.js` fails if the checked-in file has drifted.

get.description: The one file the page cannot inline: a service worker must be a real same-origin script.
Icons are drawn and PNG-encoded by `icons.js` at boot, never read from disk and never looked up by joining anything from the URL onto a path.

Cheap and always safe. `boot` echoes `RELAY_BOOT_NONCE` and is null in production: a test harness passes a nonce in and refuses to proceed until this route echoes THAT token back, which is how it tells its own child from whoever else holds the port.

The expensive one: a headline sentence, the deadman verdict, abandoned claims, response-time quantiles, the coordinator roster and (optionally) live TCP probes of the speech engines. Poll `/watch` instead if all you want is the verdict.

get.description: Deliberately separate from `/status`: this is the fallback poll and must stay cheap, so it never probes an engine. The same snapshot is pushed down the unscoped SSE stream on connect and on every change.

post.summary: "I am here"
post.description: IN MEMORY ONLY. Never logged, never replayed, and deliberately NOT evidence of life for a claim lease - only acts from inside a turn count for that (a claim, a progress note). Use `POST /tasks/{id}/progress` if you want a lease to move.

post.summary: Ask for something (the human's side)
post.description: Creates a `pending` task with `role: "user"` - the role is server-set and never taken from the client. This is the route the human's own typed and dictated messages arrive on, which is why it is the ONE write path that warns about mojibake instead of refusing it: a stored message with a `warning` block beats a dropped message. An agent making a statement should use `POST /messages` instead, which is born `done`.

instruction.description: what to do. Alias: `text`. Required UNLESS the message carries images.

text.description: alias for `instruction` - the field name the UI uses

conversationId.description: must already exist, or 400. Alias: `conversation`. Omitted = "main".

images.description: blob ids from POST /images. Validated against what has actually been uploaded.

selected.description: pre-mark a suggestion; reads back as source:"declared" so an agent never mistakes its own default for his decision

photo.summary: a photo with no caption - allowed

201.description: created. May carry a `warning` when the text contains U+FFFD - stored anyway, on purpose.

400.description: empty instruction with no images, text over 8000 chars, unknown conversationId, or a bad images/select/selected list

post.summary: Take a task, renew your own claim, or take over an expired lease
post.description:
SEND `by`. IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE CALL.

Identity is read by `claimantOf()` from `by`, then `agent`, then `author` - first non-blank string wins, trimmed and capped at 200 chars. `by` is canonical and still wins when several are sent.

THE HISTORICAL TRAP (fixed in commit fa28bfa, still live on any older deployment): this route read `body.by` ALONE, so `{"agent":"docker-coord2"}` parsed as anonymous and the route answered `200 {"status":"claimed","claimedBy":null}` - a success shape over an answer to a different question.

THE TRAP THAT IS STILL LIVE TODAY: a claim carrying NO identity at all is still accepted and still recorded as `claimedBy: null`, deliberately, because `resultTask()` warns that tightening this would break agents that answer perfectly well without ever claiming. The cost of landing there is not a missing label:

- The holder cannot renew. Renewal is `by === task.claimedBy`, and `"X" === null` is false, so the ONE agent actually doing the work is told 409 about its own task.
- A takeover records `takenOverFrom: null`, so nothing remembers anyone dropped it.
- The task never returns to `pending`, so the nudge, the pending counts and every work poll stay blind to it. The work is lost silently, for a full lease.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT CAUSES IT: `agent` is a first-class field with a DIFFERENT meaning on two neighbouring routes - `POST /conversations/{id}` (`agent` = who is seated in this tab) and `POST /conversations/{id}/activity` (`agent` = who is filing the report). One word, three routes, three meanings. Here it is merely an alias.

WHAT THE THREE OUTCOMES LOOK LIKE, all of them 200 with the task record:

- `pending` -> `claimed`, `claimedBy` set.
- already yours -> `claimedAt` refreshed. This is a renewal and is proof of life, given from inside a turn.
- held by someone else BUT the lease has expired -> taken over, recording `takenOverFrom`.

The lease is `CLAIM_LEASE_MS` (defaults to `STUCK_CLAIM_MS`) measured from the newest of `claimedAt` and `lastProgressAt`. A heartbeat does NOT move it.

requestBody.description: Optional. An empty body is valid and means an ANONYMOUS claim - see above for why you do not want one.

by.description: who is taking it. CANONICAL. Send this one.

anonymous.summary: accepted, and a mistake: 200 with claimedBy null

200.description: claimed, renewed, or taken over. The body is the task record.

anonymousClaim.summary: what the trap looks like on the wire

409.description: held by someone else and the lease has NOT expired, or the task is already done. `leaseExpiresInSec` tells "come back in a moment" apart from "this is never coming back".

post.summary: "Still here", said cheaply and repeatedly, without spending the answer
post.description:
A task accepts exactly ONE result and posting it closes the task, so an agent doing ten minutes of real work had two options: stay silent, or spend its one answer saying "not done yet". Every one of them stayed silent, and silence is the same shape as death - in one night the watchdog reported three healthy agents dead and a coordinator started a replacement on top of a working agent.

WHAT IT DOES: appends a note (newest 20 kept on the record, the event log keeps them all), refreshes the lease, and feeds `lastActedAt`.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it does not touch `result`, does not change `status`, and does not create a task - so it can never appear as backlog, be claimed, or show up in a work poll.

A BARE POST WITH NO BODY IS A VALID "still here". `note` has an alias, `text`.

OWNERSHIP, drawn exactly as narrowly as on `/result`: no `by` is fine, `by` matching the holder is fine, nothing holding it is fine. Only "I am B" about a task held by A is refused - letting the loser refresh the winner's lease would be this route causing the collision it exists to prevent.

note.description: short running commentary. Alias: `text`. Refused 400 if it contains U+FFFD.

by.description: must match the current holder if the task is claimed

200.description: noted; the lease moved; the result is still open

leaseExpiresInSec.description: proof the lease moved, so a caller can see this worked rather than assume it

400.description: note too long, not a string, or already damaged (U+FFFD)

409.description: the task is already answered (progress is only for work in flight), or someone else holds it

post.summary: Answer, closing the task. ONE SHOT.
post.description:
THE ONE-RESULT RULE IS THE SPINE OF THIS QUEUE. Posting a result sets `status: "done"` and there is no second attempt: a task that already has one answers 409 `task already has a result`. If you need to say something afterwards, `POST /messages` into the conversation.

`result` IS REQUIRED AND MUST NOT BE NULL. `{"result": null}` is refused 400, because it would produce a `done` task carrying no answer - which the relayed guard then correctly refuses to close, leaving the message permanently unanswerable. It is refused here, where it is still fixable. `result` may be any non-null JSON value; text is what the human reads.

OWNERSHIP, NARROWLY DRAWN. Four tasks in the live log are `done` with `claimedBy: null`, which is what an honour-system claim looks like from the outside.

- No `by` at all -> ALLOWED. Every existing caller keeps working, and a result may be posted straight onto a `pending` task with no claim at all.
- `by` matching the holder -> allowed.
- Nothing holds it -> allowed.
- `by` naming someone OTHER than the holder -> 409, naming the holder and the lease.

SO: TO CLEAR AN ORPHANED CLAIM - a task stuck on `claimedBy: null` from an anonymous claim, or held by an agent that is gone - OMIT `by`. Sending it is the only thing that can be refused.

AFTERWARDS: `POST /tasks/{id}/relayed`, and ONLY after this call returned 200. Never mark relayed on faith.

result.description: the answer. Any JSON value except null. Refused 400 if it contains U+FFFD.

by.description: must match the current holder if there is one. OMIT IT to answer an orphaned claim.

images.description: blob ids; stored under `resultImages` so a reference picture sent WITH the task is not overwritten by renders sent BACK

orphaned.summary: clearing a claim held by nobody - note the missing `by`

value.result: picked this up after the lease expired; done

200.description: answered. The body is the task record.

400.description: `result` missing, `result` null, damaged text, or a bad images/select list

value.error: result is null: a null answer is not an answer. Send the text the human should read.

409.description: already done, or `by` names someone other than the holder

value.hint: the lease has expired - POST /tasks/:id/claim to take it over, then post the result

post.summary: Mark an answer as delivered to the human
post.description:
NEVER CALL THIS UNTIL THE `result` POST HAS RETURNED 200. `relayed` means "the human has been shown this"; flagging it on faith is how an answer disappears from the unread counts without ever having existed.

Guarded in exactly one direction: the false -> true transition on a task with no result is refused 409. Re-flagging an already-relayed task is idempotent and keeps the ORIGINAL `relayedAt`, including for records written before the guard existed. No body.

409.description: no result yet - there is nothing to deliver

value.error: cannot mark relayed: this task has no result, so there is nothing to deliver. POST /tasks/:id/result first, and check that it returned 200 before flagging.

get.summary: The checkbox list parsed out of ONE thread entry
get.description: NOTE THE ID. This is a THREAD ENTRY id, not only a task id: `<taskId>` for the message, `<taskId>:r` for its result. Items are never stored - they are parsed out of the message text on demand, so what is ON the list (append-only text) and what is TICKED (`check` events) cannot drift apart. The index is the ordinal of the task line within the message, counting exactly as the browser counts it; a checkbox inside a fenced code block is sample text on both sides.

404.description: no such entry, or its text contains no "- [ ]" line

post.summary: Tick or untick one box, by index
post.description:
IDEMPOTENT BY VALUE: sending `on: true` twice is one state and one event, and the second call answers 200 with `changed: false`. The page retries this after being offline, and a retry must never double-toggle a box he touched once.

Unlike a `pick`, a `check` DOES reach the SSE stream (`appendEvent` maps `check` to the owning task's broadcast).

index.description: 0..total-1, the ordinal of the task line in the message

200.description: current state; `changed` says whether anything was written

400.description: index out of range, or `on` not a boolean

get.summary: The selectable image set on ONE thread entry
get.description: Same id rule as `/checks`: `<taskId>` for the message, `<taskId>:r` for the result. `decided` is true only once he has actually touched it - "nothing chosen yet" and "he chose none of them" are different answers.

404.description: the entry carries no images, or was posted with select:"none"

post.summary: Choose or unchoose one picture, by index
post.description:
Idempotent by value, like a tick. Single-select is enforced HERE rather than in the page, so his phone, his laptop and an agent all end up with the same one chosen.

TRAP: A `pick` EVENT NEVER REACHES THE SSE STREAM. `appendEvent` handles `check` explicitly but lets `pick` fall through to the task broadcast, which reads `ev.id` - and a pick event carries `entryId`, not `id`, so the lookup misses and nothing is pushed. A client watching `/events` will not learn about a choice; re-read `/picks` or the thread. (The entry's `rev` DOES move, so a `?since=<rev>` poll of `/thread` sees it.)

200.description: current selection; `changed` says whether anything was written

400.description: index out of range, or `on` not a boolean

404.description: no selectable images on that entry

get.description: `done` AND carrying a result. An agent's own message (`POST /messages`) is born `done` with no result, so it is deliberately not here. Takes the same filters as `GET /tasks`.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: anything but "false": only answers not yet marked relayed

get.description:
The read a human's page and a resuming agent both want. One task projects to ONE OR TWO entries: the message, and - if it has been answered - a second entry `<taskId>:r` carrying the result.

`since` filters on `rev`, NOT on `ts`: a tick or a pick moves an entry's `rev` without changing when it was posted, which is exactly what makes a `?since=<rev>` poll notice a checkbox. `limit` takes the LAST n - a thread is read from the end.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 or epoch ms, compared against `rev`, strictly after

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: the LAST n entries

pair.summary: one answered task, as two entries

get.summary: Read a channel OR a conversation - never both, never neither silently
get.description:
THIS ROUTE USED TO ANSWER A DIFFERENT QUESTION THAN THE ONE ASKED. `?conversationId=<tab>` was not understood, so it was dropped, and the reply was byte-for-byte the same as a bare `GET /messages`: the global `agents` channel. On 2026-08-27 an agent used it to confirm its own post had landed, got 33 rows for a tab whose conversation object said 53, none of them its own, and reported the write as failed. The write had succeeded.

So now: every selector actually filters, a selector that cannot be honoured is REFUSED rather than dropped, and the reply says what it counted. `total` is taken after `scope` and `since` narrow it and before `limit` clips it, so a complete answer is distinguishable from a clipped one. `scope.defaulted` is true when you named nothing and got the default `agents` channel.

Channel messages and conversation messages are DISJOINT STORES - a channel message is filed under the synthetic conversation `#<channel>` and belongs to no tab - so asking for both at once is malformed, not empty.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: an internal agent-to-agent channel. Defaults to `agents` when nothing is named.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: the LAST n

200.description: messages oldest first, with an explicit scope

scope.description: kind, what it includes, what it excludes, and whether the channel was defaulted

400.description: both selectors at once, a `#channel` passed as a conversation, or a bad since/limit

value.error: ask for a channel or a conversation, never both
value.why: a channel message is filed under "#agents" and belongs to no conversation, so this pair can never match anything

404.description: no conversation with that id (this used to answer 200 with the agents channel)

post.summary: An agent speaking, rather than answering
post.description:
Born `done` and `relayed: true`, with `role: "agent"` set by the server. That is the whole point: a statement is not a request, so it must not sit `pending`, must not appear in another agent's work poll, and must not count as backlog.

WHERE IT LANDS. Send `conversationId` (alias `conversation`) for the human's thread; send `channel` (or `internal: true`) for agent-to-agent traffic, which is filed under `#<channel>`, invisible to the thread and to every task query that does not name it, and CANNOT buzz his phone. Omit both and it lands in `main`.

Who is speaking: `agent`, `author` or `by`, in that order of preference.

Refused 400 if the text already contains U+FFFD - unlike `POST /tasks`, nothing the human types arrives here, so this one can afford to refuse.

channel.description: letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. Presence makes the message INTERNAL.

internal.description: true with no `channel` means the default `agents` channel

notify.description: push hint; ignored entirely for internal traffic

400.description: empty text, over 8000 chars, damaged text, unknown conversationId, bad channel name, or a bad images list

get.description: So a channel is discoverable at all. Newest-active first.
Archived tabs are HIDDEN unless asked for. Each row carries counts, the last message, and the derived liveness the page draws its badges from.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: `only` shows just the archived ones; absent, `false` or `0` hides them; any other value shows all

parameters.name: pending
parameters.description: truthy: only tabs with work waiting. The agent side's "where is there work?"

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: truthy: only tabs with answers not yet relayed

post.summary: Open a tab

agent.description: who is meant to answer here. Alias: `assignee`. relay-queue never acts on this and never spawns anything - it is a passive queue recording routing that something else decides.

400.description: missing/empty title, title over 200 chars, or `agent` not a string

post.summary: Patch a tab: seat an agent, archive it, ask it to stop
post.description:
THIS ROUTE TAKES `agent`, AND MEANS IT. That is the asymmetry that catches people: here `agent` is the FIELD - who is seated in this tab - while on `POST /tasks/{id}/claim` the field is `by` and `agent` is only an alias. Send `agent: null` (or `""`) to stand down; `assignee` is an accepted alias.

TRAP 1 - 409 "applied and then immediately overwritten". After writing, this route RE-READS the record and compares. If something else wrote to the conversation inside this request - almost always `sweepVacantChairs()` unassigning an agent that has been quiet longer than `CHAIR_VACANT_MS` - it answers 409 with `fields`, `asked`, `stored` and a `likelyCause`. NOTHING YOU ASKED FOR IS IN EFFECT. This is deliberately not a 200: a success status over a record that does not match the request is indistinguishable from the request having worked, and that ambiguity has already produced wrong conclusions. Post a message or a progress note to the tab first, then attach again.

TRAP 2 - `agentLeftReason: "presumed-gone"` IS REFUSED 400. That exact string is reserved for the vacant-chair sweep, and its entire value is that exactly one thing writes it. A caller allowed to send it could make a deliberate exit indistinguishable from an eviction. Say why in your own words: "done", "handed off", "stopping".

`agentLeftReason` only describes an agent LEAVING, so it is 400 unless this request is also clearing `agent`.

STOPPING IS ASKING, NOT KILLING. This queue cannot stop a process and never will. `stopRequested: true` answers 200 with a `stopRequestEffect` block saying so in words a UI can put on screen; the agent answers on `/conversations/{id}/stop-ack`.

ARCHIVING NAMES ITS COST. `archived: true` answers with a `ghost` warning when the tab still has a seated agent that never stood down, and with `cancelledDispatch` when a queued request naming this tab was invalidated on the way past. The default conversation `main` cannot be archived (400).

requestBody.description: At least one field, or 400 `nothing to update`.

agent.description: who is seated here. null or "" stands down. Alias: `assignee`.

agentLeftReason.description: why the seat was vacated, in the agent's own words. "presumed-gone" is refused. Only valid alongside clearing `agent`.

spawnedBy.description: which top-level session started the agent - the only thing that could actually kill it

contextFrom.description: ISO timestamp, `true` for "now", or null. The watermark a freshly seated agent reads from instead of the whole backlog. Cannot be in the future.

pendingDispatch.description: { kind, taskId } - a request about this tab currently sitting in someone's queue

200.description: the updated tab. Carries `seatRelease` when this call vacated a seat, `stopRequestEffect` when it asked for a stop, and `ghost` / `cancelledDispatch` when it archived.

400.description: nothing to update, a bad field, `agentLeftReason` without an agent leaving, `agentLeftReason: "presumed-gone"`, or archiving "main"

value.error: agentLeftReason "presumed-gone" is reserved for the vacant-chair sweep, which is what it means: nobody said they were leaving. An agent standing down on purpose should say so in its own words (e.g. "done", "handed off", "stopping").

409.description: the update was applied and then immediately overwritten inside this request. Nothing is in effect.

value.error: the update was applied and then immediately overwritten: agent
value.likelyCause: The vacant-chair sweep unassigned "old-agent" during this request, because this conversation has had no activity for longer than CHAIR_VACANT_MS. Post a message or a progress note to the conversation first, then attach again.
value.detail: Nothing you asked for is in effect. This is deliberately not a 200: a success status over a record that does not match the request is indistinguishable from the request having worked, and that ambiguity has already produced wrong conclusions.

post.summary: The agent, and only the agent, answering a stop request
post.description:
`stopping` = winding down, `stopped` = finished. A `stopped` conversation cannot go back to `stopping` (409).

`stopped` also stands the agent down in the same write, recording `agentLeft`, `agentLeftAt` and `agentLeftReason: "stopped"` - the invariant is that an `agent` going from a name to null ALWAYS records who left, whichever door it went through.

`worktrees` are REPORTED, NEVER VERIFIED: this server does not touch git and cannot know whether they were released. The reply says so with `worktreesAreSelfReported: true`.

value.note: handed off to the merge worker

400.description: phase is neither "stopping" nor "stopped", or worktrees is not an array

409.description: already stopped; a stopped agent cannot go back to stopping

get.summary: What the coordinator in this tab is doing
get.description: NEWEST FIRST - a panel opens on what just happened, not on history. Subagents are folded into a roster here rather than in the browser: one is "running" until a `finished` with the same name arrives, and one that never finishes stays visible forever, on purpose. `reporting` carries the difference between "quiet" and "not instrumented".

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: clamped to ACTIVITY_CAP (200)

post.summary: A coordinator narrating its own work
post.description:
THIS ROUTE TAKES `agent` AS A REAL FIELD - here it means WHO IS REPORTING, which is a third meaning of the word (see `POST /tasks/{id}/claim` and `POST /conversations/{id}`). `subagent` is who the entry is ABOUT.

Deliberately tiny and deliberately optional: an agent that reports nothing behaves exactly as it does today.

`spawned` and `finished` are DURABLE (written to the event log and replayed); `tool` and `note` live only in the in-memory ring and are lost on restart.

BACKFILL IS MARKED, NEVER SILENT. Pass `at` to record when a subagent really started - a coordinator resumed mid-flight otherwise reports an hour-old worker as `runningForSec: 10`, which is a plausible number that is wrong. A supplied `at` is validated and REJECTED rather than clamped (more than 5s in the future, or older than the feed keeps), and the entry is flagged `reconstructed: true`.

subagent.description: REQUIRED for `spawned` and `finished`, so the panel can pair the two halves

task.description: what the subagent was asked to do

durable.description: false for `tool` and `note`: in-memory only, lost on restart

400.description: unknown kind, spawned/finished with no subagent, or an unparseable/future/too-old `at`

get.summary: Publication state and a preflight of what would go public
get.description: `live: false` is said out loud in the API because it is the whole design: a share COPIES, it does not proxy, so the link works when this machine is off. `preflight` counts the entries, images and bytes that would be published and runs a secret scan over them - read `findings` before you publish.

configured.description: false when data/share.json is missing - publishing will 503

post.summary: Publish or refresh the public snapshot
post.description:
RE-POSTING IS HOW YOU REFRESH. It keeps the SAME slug, so a link already sent to someone keeps working and simply shows newer content.

Images are pulled off disk and inlined as data URIs within a byte budget; anything that does not fit is reported as `imagesOmitted`. The reply repeats the secret-scan `findings`.

503.description: sharing is not configured (data/share.json is missing or incomplete)

delete.description:
DELETES THE PUBLISHED PAGE AND FORGETS THE SLUG.

AND THE SLUG DOES NOT COME BACK. `publishRoute` reuses the existing slug only while the share RECORD exists; revoking drops it, so the next publish mints a NEW slug at a NEW url, and every copy of the old link - in a text message, in someone's bookmarks - is permanently dead.

So: to refresh a share, POST again. Only DELETE when you actually want the page gone.

404.description: no such conversation, or it is not shared

503.description: sharing is not configured, so the remote page cannot be deleted

get.summary: THE ONE STICKY LIST FOR A TAB (singular - read this)
get.description:
SINGULAR ON PURPOSE, AND ONE LETTER FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT SYSTEM.

- `/checklist` (THIS ONE): the single editable, pinned list belonging to a conversation. Items have generated IDS, can be added, edited, removed and imported, and are ticked by id via `/checklist/tick`.
- `/checklists` (PLURAL): a read-only projection of every `- [ ]` list PARSED OUT OF MESSAGE TEXT anywhere in the queue. Items have ORDINALS, not ids, are immutable, and are ticked by index via `POST /tasks/{entryId}/checks`.

They are genuinely different objects. Nothing written to one appears in the other, except through the explicit `importFrom` on `POST /checklist`.

`list` is `null` rather than an empty list when the tab has none: "no list here" and "a list with nothing left on it" are different answers and a coordinator acts differently on each.

parameters.name: conversation
parameters.description: REQUIRED (400 without it). Alias: `conversationId`.

400.description: no conversation named

post.summary: Create or update the tab's list - every operation named explicitly
post.description:
The coordinator's write path. NOTHING HERE REPLACES THE LIST WHOLESALE: a coordinator that meant to add one chore and instead cleared fifteen ticks would be worse than the fragmentation this feature fixes. So there is no "items" field - only `add`, `edit`, `remove`, `importFrom`, `clearDone` and `title`.

Order of operations: removals, then edits, then adds, then imports, then `clearDone`. Removing and re-adding an id in one call therefore works.

EDITING KEEPS THE TICK but not the pretence it was earned against the new words: the old wording is kept as `tickedText` and the item reads back `editedSinceTicked: true`.

`importFrom` copies the OPEN items out of a message-parsed checklist (the `/checklists` world) into this one, records the source, and skips duplicates by text - so importing twice does not double the list. Ticked items are deliberately left behind.

Max 200 items, 500 chars each.

add.description: a string, an object {text}, or an array of either

edit.description: { id, text }, or an array of them. 404 if an id is gone.

remove.description: an item id, or an array of them. Unknown ids are silently ignored.

importFrom.description: a THREAD ENTRY id (or an array), whose parsed `- [ ]` items are copied in

200.description: the whole list, after the change

400.description: no conversationId, bad text, or more than 200 items

404.description: unknown conversation, an `edit` id that is gone, or an `importFrom` entry with no checklist

post.summary: Tick one item of the tab list, BY ID
post.description:
Its own route because it is the call that happens constantly, and because it must never be able to rewrite item text. Idempotent by value: ticking an already-ticked item answers 200 `changed: false`.

A 404 for an unknown id names the ids that ARE there, because an id that is gone is nearly always an item somebody removed, and a client that only learns "404" retries it forever.

This is the SINGULAR system. To tick a box inside a message, use `POST /tasks/{entryId}/checks` with an INDEX instead.

id.description: the item id from GET /checklist. Alias: `itemId`.

400.description: `on` is not a boolean, or a field is not a string

404.description: no list on that conversation, or no such item id

get.summary: Every list PARSED OUT OF MESSAGE TEXT (plural - read this too)
get.description:
PLURAL, AND NOT THE SAME SYSTEM AS `/checklist`. This is the read-only projection of every `- [ ]` list found in message and result text across the queue: derived from immutable text, addressed by ORDINAL, ticked through `POST /tasks/{entryId}/checks`. The singular `/checklist` is the editable pinned list belonging to a tab, addressed by generated IDS.

Answers "what is on his list right now" in one call, without parsing the thread.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: truthy: only lists with something left

get.summary: Every selectable image set, or those in one conversation
get.description: "What has he chosen", answerable in one call without the thread. `decided: false` means he has not touched it yet, which is NOT the same as choosing none.

parameters.name: undecided
parameters.description: truthy: only sets he has not touched

get.summary: Balance and history of the flat one-credit-per-feature economy

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: history rows; a non-integer or negative value is 400

post.summary: Award credits for chores done
post.description: Atomic by construction: no `await` sits between reading the balance and writing the event that changes it, so no other request can interleave.

reason.description: required. Refused if it contains U+FFFD.

400.description: amount not a positive integer, or reason missing/too long/damaged

post.summary: Spend exactly one credit
post.description: The cost is ALWAYS exactly 1 and cannot be read from the body - a caller cannot ask to spend more or less than the one credit a feature costs. 402 when the balance is 0.

400.description: reason missing, too long, or damaged

get.summary: The roster, the tree and the graveyard
get.description: `confirmedDead` and `presumedDead` are kept apart in the payload so no client has to invent the split, and so "confirmed" and "presumed" cannot be summed into one number.

post.summary: Register a name, and get the key that proves you own it
post.description:
The reply carries a `key`. KEEP IT: `POST /agents/{name}` refuses without it, and resuming the same name after a restart requires it.

Names are compared FOLDED, so two spellings that cannot be told apart cannot both exist - a 409 names the holder and suggests a free name, because an agent told only "taken" tends to try one more variant that folds to the same thing.

task.description: what it is here to do

parent.description: who spawned it - builds the tree

key.description: required to RESUME an existing name

200.description: resumed an existing name with the right key

201.description: registered; the body carries the key

400.description: bad name, bad field, or unknown conversationId

409.description: that name (or one that folds to it) is held by someone else

429.description: too many registered agents; nothing is removed automatically

500.description: the inbox file could not be created

get.summary: One agent, with its death verdict

post.summary: "This is what I am doing now" - requires the key
post.description: The act that proves life, so it also refreshes `lastActedAt`. REQUIRES the `key` from registration (403 without it): a roster where anyone can rewrite what another agent claims to be working on is worse than no roster, because it looks authoritative.

400.description: a bad field, or an unknown conversationId

get.description: For a resumed agent catching up. `wake` carries the recipe for how this agent is actually woken, and `file` names the JSONL on disk it is tailing.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: truthy: only messages not yet acked

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: the LAST n; defaults to 100, clamped to 500

post.summary: Write a line into an agent's inbox
post.description: The reply says `acknowledged: false` and NOT "delivered", deliberately: the line is in the file, but whether anything is tailing it is not something this server can see, and claiming otherwise would rebuild the lie the ack exists to expose. It counts as picked up only when the agent posts an ack.

201.description: written to the inbox - NOT confirmed read

400.description: empty or over-long text

500.description: the inbox file could not be opened or appended to

post.summary: "I have this" - the only report of a read anything can trust
post.description: Written, delivered and READ are three different states, and only the agent can report the third. Acking happens inside a turn, so it also counts as proof of life. Idempotent: a second ack answers 200 with `already: true`.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: the `id` from the inbox

404.description: no such agent, or no such message in its inbox

post.summary: Report that an agent is done - confirmed death, not presumed
post.description: Only the agent itself (with its key) or its recorded parent may file this. `lastWords` is what it wanted the record to say.

by.description: the parent, if the parent is reporting

400.description: a bad field

403.description: only the agent or its parent may report this

post.summary: Bring an agent back out of the graveyard
post.description: For the case where an agent was presumed dead and is demonstrably not. Answers 200 with an explanation when there was nothing to exhume.

400.description: a bad note

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: defaults to 200, clamped to 500

post.summary: Upload image BYTES (not JSON) and get back a blob id
post.description:
POST THE RAW BYTES: `curl --data-binary @file.png`. This is not a JSON route and there is no multipart parser.

THE FORMAT IS READ FROM THE BYTES; the content-type header is IGNORED. Unrecognised bytes are 415, and the refusal says so explicitly, because a caller who set content-type correctly and was still refused will otherwise blame the header.

The id is the sha256 of the content, so re-posting identical bytes is a no-op and `deduplicated` says it happened. Metadata rides in the QUERY STRING, not the body.

parameters.name: alt
parameters.description: the label an agent should quote back at him

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: who uploaded it

400.description: empty body, unknown conversationId, or a bad alt/agent

415.description: these bytes are not an image format this server recognises

500.description: the bytes could not be written to disk

get.description:
Immutable caching is honest here in a way it almost never is: the name IS the hash of the content, so this URL can never mean different bytes. Served with a year-long immutable cache, `nosniff`, `content-disposition: inline` and a `default-src 'none'; sandbox` CSP - nothing served here may act as a document.

410 (not 404) when the log remembers the image but the bytes are gone from disk: a restored DATA_DIR without its images directory is a different problem from a wrong id, and a placeholder would leave him looking at a broken square with no way to tell it from a bug.

404.description: not a 64-character sha256, or no such image

410.description: in the log, but the bytes are no longer on disk

head.description: Same route, same statuses, no body.

404.description: not an image id, or no such image

get.summary: Every record carrying a replacement character. A SURVEY, NOT A REPAIR.
get.description:
IT NEVER REPAIRS. A U+FFFD could have been an em-dash, an accented letter, a quotation mark or an emoji, and nothing left in the record says which. Guessing one and writing it into an append-only archive would turn a visible gap into an invisible fabrication - a known unknown can be resolved by asking the author, an invention cannot.

`byAuthor` is the useful column: it says whose client is still sending bad bytes.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: defaults to 200, clamped to 1000

get.summary: Server-Sent Events. WATCH, DO NOT POLL.
get.description:
`text/event-stream`, a `retry:` hint, a `: connected` comment, and a `: ping` comment every few seconds to hold the connection open.

SCOPE IT. With `?conversation=<id>` the server filters to that tab's own events. WITHOUT a query parameter this is the FULL FIREHOSE across every conversation - see `/events/firehose` for the same thing under an unmistakable name. An unscoped connection also receives the `watch` snapshot immediately on connect, so a page opening into an already-stranded state sees it at once; a scoped one does not, because global health has no conversationId to match the filter against.

WHAT NEVER ARRIVES HERE: internal channel traffic (an agent reads its channel by polling); push subscription changes; share/unshare; credits; AND `pick` EVENTS, which fall through the dispatch in `appendEvent` and are silently dropped. `check` events DO arrive.

Frames are `data: {"now":..., "conversationId":..., "entries":[...]}` for thread changes, `{"conversation":{...}}` for tab changes, and `{"watch":{...}}` for the deadman verdict.

get.summary: The unscoped everything-stream, under a name that cannot be reached for by accident
get.description: Byte-for-byte what bare `GET /events` with no query string already gives. It exists so that reaching for "the events stream" does not land a coordinator on the expensive firehose without meaning to. ANY query string here is IGNORED: there is no way to make `/events/firehose` scoped, on purpose.

post.summary: Raw PCM in, transcript out
post.description:
POST the raw audio bytes (not JSON, not a WAV): signed 16-bit little-endian PCM, mono. The body must be a whole number of frames.

The transcript is repaired against the `/terms` dictionary HERE rather than in the page, so every caller of `/stt` gets it - and `raw` comes back alongside `text` so a composer can offer one-tap undo. `corrections` lists what was changed.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: int16 only

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: mono only

400.description: no audio, a partial frame, or a bad rate/width/channels

502.description: the speech engine could not be reached or returned nothing

post.summary: Text in, a spoken WAV out
post.description:
A dumb primitive, exactly like `/stt`: it speaks what it is given and knows nothing about the conversation. Deciding WHAT is worth listening to (stripping URLs, collapsing code blocks) belongs to the page, where it can be seen and tuned.

WAV rather than raw PCM because the browser has to decode it: a 44-byte header is the difference between `decodeAudioData` working everywhere and hand-rolling a PCM reader. `x-audio-ms` and `x-took-ms` ride in the headers, since a binary body cannot carry them.

400.description: empty text, or text too long to speak

502.description: the text-to-speech engine returned no audio

get.summary: The vocabulary dictionary /stt repairs transcripts against
get.description:
Two files merged: the curated `stt-terms.json` in the read-only checkout, and the overlay in DATA_DIR that `POST /terms` appends to. The reply reports `overlay` separately so "did my POST land" is one read rather than a diff against twenty other terms.

When the curated file is missing or invalid, repair is DISABLED entirely and this answers 200 with `repair: "disabled"` and empty lists - not an error, because a broken dictionary must never take the transcript with it.

protect.description: ordinary language that must never be rewritten

repair.description: present ONLY when the dictionary is unusable

post.summary: Teach the dictionary a word, or a mishearing of one
post.description:
The channel a coordinator actually has. "Add a term, save, done" assumes an editor on this machine; the coordinator guard denies every write but markdown, and denies node/python/sed -i - so this route is the way in. Writes to the DATA_DIR overlay, never to the curated file, which sits inside a read-only bind mount.

THE MERGE IS ADDITIVE ONLY. Nothing posted here can delete a `heard` form, unprotect a word, or overwrite a note a human deliberately wrote down - a `note` is APPENDED, and only if the merged note does not already contain it, so a retry is a no-op rather than a second copy.

EVERY 400 HERE IS A FORM THAT WOULD BE STORED AND THEN SILENTLY IGNORED, which is worse than a rejection: the caller believes the mishearing is fixed and it keeps happening. Refused: a `heard` form with no `term` to belong to; a form that normalises to its own term (`loadTerms` drops those); a form longer than `maxSpanWords`; a form already in `protect` (listed forms bypass protect, so this would quietly start rewriting ordinary language); a form already owned by a different term; a `protect` entry that is already canonical or already a listed mishearing.

Read `changed` in the reply: an add that merged into nothing must not read the same as one that changed the dictionary. `dictionary` counts come from the RELOADED index, so the reply proves repair is actually using the write rather than that a file was written.

term.description: the canonical spelling. Required if `heard` is present.

heard.description: mishearings that should be corrected TO `term`

protect.description: ordinary words repair must never rewrite

note.description: appended to the existing note, never replacing it

200.description: processed. `changed: false` means it merged into nothing.

created.description: new to the DICTIONARY, not merely to the overlay file

400.description: nothing to add, or a form that would be stored and then ignored - the message says which

500.description: the overlay file is not valid JSON, or could not be written

503.description: the curated dictionary is missing or invalid, so there is nothing to add to

post.summary: One diagnostic line from the browser into the container log
post.description: The UI's real home is a phone, where nobody can open a devtools console, so "the mic did nothing" is otherwise undebuggable. DIAGNOSTICS ONLY: nothing is stored, nothing enters the event log, and it cannot affect the queue. Newlines and control characters are flattened so untrusted text cannot forge extra log lines. Rate limited to 60 lines a minute; over that it answers HTTP 429 with `{ ok: false }`.

get.summary: Quiet hours, subscribed devices and the VAPID public key

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: scopes the snapshot to one device

post.summary: Change quiet hours

tz.description: an IANA zone this machine knows

400.description: unknown timezone, a time that is not "HH:MM", or nothing to change

post.summary: Arm this browser for web push
post.description: Takes a standard PushSubscription. A second subscription with the same endpoint replaces the first rather than doubling it.

ua.description: used only to label the device

400.description: missing/insecure endpoint, or unusable keys

503.description: push is disabled on this server (no VAPID keys)

post.summary: Disarm a device
Send a test notification to every armed device

503.description: push is disabled on this server

get.description:
A BOUNDED, ADDITIVE experiment, not a migration: a second app (Hono + @hono/zod-openapi) mounted under `/v2`, covering exactly 5 routes. Everything under `/v2` is checked first and unconditionally - nothing below it in the router ever sees a `/v2` request - and every v1 route is untouched.

The v2 routes do NOT reimplement anything: they validate and document the request, then hand off to the SAME `claimTask`/`resultTask`/`progressTask`/`relayTask`/`applyFilters` functions through a `res` shim, so the mutation logic cannot drift. See HONO-POC.md.

get.summary: The GENERATED spec for the 5 POC routes only
get.description: OpenAPI 3.0.0, generated from the zod route definitions. Do not confuse it with `/openapi.json`, which is this hand-written document and covers the whole server.
Only `conversation`/`conversationId` and `status` are wired up here; channel/unread/expired/since/limit exist on v1 and are intentionally out of scope. Served by the same `applyFilters()` v1 uses.

post.summary: POC mirror of POST /tasks/{id}/claim
post.description: Delegates to the same `claimTask()`, so every trap on the v1 route applies here unchanged. The body is parsed by hand rather than by Hono's validator, because that validator treats an EMPTY body as malformed JSON and a bare claim must stay valid.

409.description: already claimed (lease not expired) or already done

post.summary: POC mirror of POST /tasks/{id}/result
post.description: Delegates to the same `resultTask()`, including the "result is required" / "result is null" distinction from a malformed-JSON 400.

400.description: result missing or null, or bad images/select

409.description: already done, or held by a different claimant

post.summary: POC mirror of POST /tasks/{id}/relayed

409.description: no result yet - nothing to deliver

post.summary: POC mirror of POST /tasks/{id}/progress
post.description: A bare POST with no body is a valid "still here", exactly as on v1.

200.description: noted; lease renewed; result still open

409.description: already answered, or held by a different claimant

entryId.name: id
entryId.description: a THREAD ENTRY id: `<taskId>` for the message, `<taskId>:r` for its result

agentName.name: name
agentName.description: the agent's registered name; matched folded, so spellings that cannot be told apart resolve to the same agent

conversation.name: conversation
conversation.description: filter to one conversation. Canonical spelling.

since.name: since
since.description: ISO 8601 or epoch milliseconds. STRICTLY after. A value this server cannot parse is a 400, never a silent no-op.

BadRequest.description: a malformed request. The message names the field.

Error.description: Every refusal on this server. `error` is always a sentence a human can act on; the extra keys vary by route and are documented on the operation that returns them - a 409 from `/claim` carries `leaseExpiresInSec`, a 409 from `POST /conversations/{id}` carries `asked` and `stored`, and a UTF-8 refusal carries `detail` naming the first bad byte.

detail.description: on a UTF-8 refusal: where the bytes went wrong, so the caller does not retry the identical body

examples.error: the request body is not valid UTF-8, so nothing was stored

Counts.description: Queue depth. Internal channel traffic is never counted - agent chatter is not backlog.

unrelayed.description: answered but not yet marked delivered

Task.description:
THE RECORD EVERY WRITE PATH PRODUCES. A human's request (`POST /tasks`, `role: "user"`, born `pending`) and an agent's statement (`POST /messages`, `role: "agent"`, born `done` and `relayed`) are the same shape in the same log - which is why the thread projection, the replay and the live stream handle both with no special case.

Optional fields appear only when something has touched them, so a plain record is byte-for-byte the shape every client was written against. Additional properties are expected.

conversationId.description: absent on the oldest records, which read as "main"

role.description: SERVER-SET from the route used, never taken from the client

to.description: on agent messages: who it is addressed to

claimedBy.description: NULL ON A CLAIMED TASK MEANS AN ANONYMOUS CLAIM - a seat that reads occupied with nobody in it. See POST /tasks/{id}/claim.

takenOverFrom.description: who held it before an expired-lease takeover

result.description: any JSON value. Null means unanswered; it can never be SET to null.

relayed.description: the human has been shown the answer

progress.description: the newest 20 progress notes; the event log keeps them all

lastProgressAt.description: feeds the claim lease alongside claimedAt

images.description: blob ids attached to the MESSAGE

resultImages.description: blob ids attached to the ANSWER - deliberately a separate set

warning.description: only from POST /tasks: the text contains U+FFFD and was stored anyway

Message.description: A message as `GET /messages` returns it - the channel's own view, with no queue machinery. `role`, `status` and `answered` are here for the CONVERSATION read, where a human's message is a real task that may still be waiting: rendering it identically to a statement is how a reader concludes nobody has said anything.

channel.description: set on internal traffic, null in a conversation

ThreadEntry.description:
ONE TASK PROJECTS TO ONE OR TWO OF THESE: the message, and - once answered - a reply entry whose id is `<taskId>:r`. Nothing is stored in this shape; it is derived, which is why flags like `damaged` light up retroactively on records written years before the flag existed.

`rev` IS THE FIELD TO POLL ON. It is the newest of the entry's own timestamps AND of every tick and pick on it, so `?since=<rev>` notices a checkbox that changed nothing else. `ts` does not move.

text.description: a non-string result is JSON-stringified into this

author.description: added only when there is one

claimedBy.description: added only when something holds it

checklist.description: { total, done, items } when the text contains a task list

selection.description: { mode, total, picked, decided, items } when the entry carries selectable images

Conversation.description:
A TAB. Every task belongs to exactly one; records written before conversations existed replay into `main`.

The stop fields are the honest half of a control this server cannot actually perform: relay-queue can ASK an agent to stop and can record that it answered, but it cannot kill a process and never will. `spawnedBy` names the only session that could, and is null unless something told us - never inferred, because a guess here puts a confident button in front of a process nobody can reach.

agent.description: who is SEATED here. Set with `agent` on POST /conversations/{id} - note that the claim route calls this same idea `by`.

agentSince.description: when the chair was filled. NOT evidence of life; only the vacant-chair sweep should read it.

agentLeftReason.description: in the agent's own words. `presumed-gone` is written ONLY by the sweep and is refused from callers.

stopAck.description: written by the agent from inside a turn. null = not heard from since the request, which is normal, not an error.

worktrees.description: SELF-REPORTED. This server does not touch git.

contextFrom.description: the watermark a freshly seated agent reads from. null = never cleared, which is NOT the same as cleared at the beginning.

contextMarks.description: every watermark ever set, so a tab cleared five times draws five session dividers instead of losing four

pendingDispatch.description: { kind, at, taskId } - a request about this tab sitting in someone's queue. Archiving cancels it in the same write.

missing.description: the tab was inferred from tasks that name it, and was never created

Term.description: One entry in the speech dictionary: a canonical spelling and the mishearings that should be corrected to it. Matching is phonetic (a trimmed Metaphone), which is why short terms are never matched by sound - "cold", "called" and "clot" are all phonetically identical to "Claude".

heard.description: forms the engine produces instead. A form equal to its own term is dropped at load.

note.description: why. APPENDED to, never replaced - the reasoning for a decision is how a term stays explainable.

EntryChecklist.description: A checklist PARSED OUT OF MESSAGE TEXT (the `/checklists` plural world). Items are addressed by INDEX and cannot be edited: a corrected list is a new message, which correctly starts with fresh ticks. `source` tells "he ticked it" apart from "it was written already ticked".

supersededBy.description: the tab list that imported these items, if any

TabList.description: THE ONE STICKY LIST for a conversation (the `/checklist` singular world). Items have generated IDS and are ticked by id. `editedSinceTicked` is true when an item was reworded after it was ticked - the tick survives, but not the pretence it was earned against these words.

importedFrom.description: thread entry ids whose open items were copied in

tickedText.description: the wording that was actually ticked

PickList.description: A selectable image set hanging off one thread entry. `mode: "one"` is enforced SERVER-SIDE, so his phone, his laptop and an agent all end up with the same single choice.

decided.description: true only once he has actually touched it. "nothing chosen yet" is not "he chose none".

source.description: `declared` is the poster's own suggestion, NOT his decision

ImageRef.description: An image as it appears inside a thread entry.

path.description: where the bytes are on the host, for tools that read the disk

Image.description: A gallery record. `blob` is the sha256 of the bytes and is what `/images/{blob}` serves; `id` identifies this POST of them, so the same bytes uploaded twice are one blob and two records.

ActivityEntry.description: One line of a coordinator narrating its own work. `reconstructed` is the honest flag: true = the caller supplied `at` (backfill), false = server-stamped, null = the record predates the field.

InboxMessage.description: A line in an agent's addressed inbox. `ackedAt` is the only trustworthy report of a read, because only the agent can write it.
